days.label: Monday
days.text: Monday is quieter than the rest of the week, which makes it a good night to try something small. Readers can drop into Shakespeare Out Loud in the Local History Room at Fletcher Free from 4 to 5:30, where a group reads Romeo and Juliet aloud, take a part or just listen. Burlington Parks needs hands for a phragmites pull at North Beach from 3 to 6, drop in anytime, bring work gloves and closed toe shoes. Language lovers have Spanish Chat Mondays at Three Needs from 7 to 8, all levels welcome. If you would rather throw things, pickup dodgeball runs at the Miller Center from 7 to 8:15, no team required, $5 a game. The quieter crowd can pick between the Burlington Dharma Collective's Monday Night Live at Outright Vermont from 7 to 8:30, a talk, a meditation and a group discussion, free with donations accepted, or a guided meditation class [MEETUP] with teacher Laura McPeake at the Burlington Friends Meeting House from 6:30 to 8, $10. Makers can join the Collage Collective at Expressive Arts Burlington on Flynn Ave from 6:30 to 9, and the Anime Group meets at Pathways Vermont's Morgan's Place from 6 to 8. Up in Colchester, the Historical Society hosts History of Colchester Schools at 828 Main Street from 7 to 8:30, a photo talk on the town's early schoolhouses, free, use the back porch entrance.

days.label: Tuesday
days.text: Tuesday is the biggest show of the week. Marcus King Band ($63-109.25) plays the Flynn Main Stage at 8, King reunited with his longtime live band for the first time since 2018 with the new album Darling Blue on the way, and tickets are down to limited availability. Before that, the VSO's Andrew Crust and Matt LaRocca host Scheherazade on the Rocks at the Venetian Soda Lounge from 7 to 8, a happy hour walk through the stories behind the orchestra's season opener, sliding scale tickets with snacks included and a cash bar, only 50 spots. Dinner has a cause, since American Flatbread's Benefit Bake for the Intervale Center runs from 4 to 10 with part of the proceeds from every flatbread going to the Intervale. On the waterfront, Montreal psych band Elephant Stone with Carinae ($18 adv) plays Foam, doors at 7:30 and show at 8, and Deadheads have Dead Is Alive with Dobbs' Dead ($15) at Einstein's at 8. Artists can walk into the Vermont Figure Drawing Collective at Karma Bird House from 6 to 8, $20 cash, live models. French speakers meet for Pause-Café Mardi at Burlington Bay from 5 to 7, and anyone can sit with Community Meditation at the Unitarian Universalist Society at 152 Pearl from 5:15 to 6, free with donations accepted. Trivia people can head to Colchester for the Forever 38 group's trivia night at Burger Bar [MEETUP] from 7 to 9. Parents with kids can hit Craftytown at the South Burlington Public Library from 3 to 4.

days.label: Wednesday
days.text: Wednesday, so early birds can catch the South District Mayor Meetup with Mayor Mulvaney-Stanak at Zero Gravity from 8 to 9 AM, any district welcome, or roll through Walk and Bike to Work Day at Jake's ONE Market from 7:30 to 9 AM, where Local Motion has free goodies and discounts on breakfast and coffee. And of course we have Pick-up Basketball [MEETUP] runs at Pomeroy Park at 5:30, outdoors, competitive. Winooski owns the evening with Winooski Pride at Rotary Park from 5 to 8, free, with music and food, bound to be a good time! A short walk away Michael Perry plays acoustic originals and covers at 4 Quarters from 7 to 9, free. The Fleming Museum throws its Fall Kickoff Party from 5 to 7, also free, and Vermont Humanities hosts a free afternoon discussion on Charity, Sylvia and the VSO with composer Clarice Assad at the UVM Recital Hall from 2 to 4, registration required. Downtown, passeggiata fills Church Street with the Italian evening stroll at 6 and the All-Inclusive Dyke-Tacular takes over Doma Bar on Pine Street from 5 to 10. Deaf Friendly Trivia Night at Citizen Cider runs from 6:30 to 8:30 with an ASL interpreter, and Generator's free Hobby to Business Workshop goes from 6 to 8, preregister. Comedy fans get $5 Improv Night at Vermont Comedy Club at 7, guest team Technical Difficulties, and jazz fans get free Jazz Night with Ray Vega at Hotel Vermont at 8:30. Two touring shows are worth the ticket, folk songwriter John Craigie with Humbird ($30-35) in the Higher Ground Ballroom, doors at 7 and show at 8, running low on tickets, and harpist Mikaela Davis with Johanna Samuels ($20 adv) at Foam at 7:30. Runners can join the 5K run from Zero Gravity [MEETUP] at 5:30 with a hang at the taproom after, and volunteers can spend the afternoon tending Rock Point starting at 3:30, gardening and trail work, pre-register.

days.label: Thursday
days.text: Thursday, we have our own Btown Bites at Bluebird Barbecue [MEETUP] is our 21 to 35 dinner group, meeting at the restaurant on Riverside Ave at 6. Have a great waitlist, so definitely plan on doing more of these. Dog people should not miss the last Bark and Brew of the season ($20) at the Humane Society of Chittenden County from 5:30 to 7:30, two drinks included, with Foam, Weird Window and Black Flannel pouring, Le Bon Gout on food, and dogs welcome but not required. The shelter is also waiving adoption fees for every animal 6 months and older from Tuesday through the 22nd. South Burlington's Park Hop Brews lands at The Overlook at Underwood Park from 5:30 to 7:30 with Red Hot Juba, food vendors, and a free paint and sip. Music runs all night, with the free Hot Pickin' Party bluegrass trio at Foam at 7, Brooklyn indie rockers Gooseberry ($15-20) at the Higher Ground Showcase Lounge with Girls Night, doors at 7, the Summer Concert Series on the patio at Folino's in Williston at 6, and Vinyl Thursdays at Hotel Vermont at 6. The Burlington Baroque Festival opens its third year at College Street Congregational Church at 7:30 with the period orchestra L'Harmonie des saisons and Boston's Blue Heron, $40 to 80, $10 for students. Film people can see 'The Passion of Joan of Arc' ($6-12) at the Film House at Main Street Landing at 7, the 1928 silent with a live improvised score from Michael Chorney's Freeway Clyde. Readers can meet author Libby Cataldi at Phoenix Books from 6:30 to 7:30 for her Italian American memoir, and thinkers can catch Dr. Marc Watkins on human agency in the age of AI at Saint Michael's McCarthy Arts Center at 7, with a Q&A after. Homebuyers get straight answers at the Seven Days House Party at Wilder Wines at 6, a free workshop with a lender, a Realtor and a lawyer taking questions, register ahead. Trivia is at Butter Bar with Don Mahogany at 7, LGBTQ+ folks have Out in the 802's happy hour at Lincoln's [MEETUP] from 5 to 7, the speakeasy off Church Street near Red Square, and Vermont Ultimate's fall rec league kicks off at Landry Park in Winooski from 7 to 9, $50 for the season or $40 for new players. Early risers can join the BTV Clean Up Crew at the top of Church Street from 7:30 to 10 AM, bring your own gloves. And Sunset Watchers Club might pop up somewhere at sunset this week, they announce the spot a day or two ahead on Instagram .
